title: DeepScientist: Advancing Frontier-Pushing Scientific Findings Progressively
claim: Progress that took human researchers years is matched and surpassed by our autonomous system in days, beating state-of-the-art baselines.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shared y-axis, year vs day x-axes
description: A two-panel line chart shares one y-axis, RAID AUROC score. The left panel, titled Human Expert Researchers, plots the years 2019–2025 on the x-axis. Gray square markers connected by lines show zero-shot human methods (Log-Perplexity, Log-Rank, LRR, Fast-Detect, Binoculars, Glimpse). A light-gray line shows supervised methods (RoBERTa-base, RADAR). Red method names with black venue labels annotate the points. Horizontal dashed lines mark the supervised and zero-shot SoTA levels. The right panel, DeepScientist, uses days 1–15 on the x-axis. A thick orange line with diamond markers and a shaded band climbs from the prior baseline through T-Detect, TDT and PA-Detect, with arrows pointing at each. It passes both SoTA lines. Red stars carry italic milestone notes at 3, 11 and 14 days. The eye goes first to the bright orange curve on the tinted right panel.
caption: Comparison of research progress timelines for AI text detection on the RAID [ref]. The right panel shows that DeepScientist achieves progress in two weeks that is comparable to three years of human research [ref] (left panel). All zero-shot methods, including the system-generated T-Detect, TDT, and PA-Detect, uniformly adopt Falcon-7B [ref] as the base model. Additionally, all methods produced by DeepScientist demonstrate higher throughput than the previous SOTA method, Binoculars [ref].
abstract: While previous AI Scientist systems can generate novel findings, they often lack the focus to produce scientifically valuable contributions that address pressing human-defined challenges. We introduce DeepScientist, a system designed to overcome this by conducting goal-oriented, fully autonomous scientific discovery over month-long timelines. It formalizes discovery as a Bayesian Optimization problem, operationalized through a hierarchical evaluation process consisting of "hypothesize, verify, and analyze". Leveraging a cumulative Findings Memory, this loop intelligently balances the exploration of novel hypotheses with exploitation, selectively promoting the most promising findings to higher-fidelity levels of validation. Consuming over 20,000 GPU hours, the system generated about 5,000 unique scientific ideas and experimentally validated approximately 1100 of them, ultimately surpassing human-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods on three frontier AI tasks by 183.7\%, 1.9\%, and 7.9\%. This work provides the first large-scale evidence of an AI achieving discoveries that progressively surpass human SOTA on scientific tasks, producing valuable findings that genuinely push the frontier of scientific discovery. To facilitate further research into this process, we will open-source all experimental logs and system code at https://github.com/ResearAI/DeepScientist/.
